notes: Nill Download Manager 2.0.9 is a correctness release that grew out of a screen recording of a real 2.0.8 video download whose numbers did not tell the truth. Video progress now counts real bytes: the reported total no longer grows together with the downloaded amount — a 24 MB video could previously sail past 110 MB on the counter while pinned at 100% — and the percentage means what it says in the card, the dialog and the saved journal. Time-left figures are marked "~" until at least 256 KB over 10 seconds makes them worth trusting, a starting download shows its steps — resolving, probing, starting — instead of one opaque "Preparing…", and the card declares "Finishing…" only once the numbers have actually settled. Relaunching inside a scheduled window no longer replays the whole queue on every launch, queued downloads start promptly instead of stalling, and a browser hand-off can no longer be lost if the browser restarts its extension worker at the wrong moment. The native host now follows the browser's own cookie rules — host-only cookies stay on their host and path boundaries are respected — and two running copies of NDM can no longer process the same browser offer twice or splice each other's saved progress into a corrupt file. The quality picker now quotes the size of the format that will actually download, so the size beside a quality is the size of the file you get. A finished video's Open Folder reveals the merged file itself, and the extension-update notice is tied to the version it was dismissed for, so it warns again when it should. 2.0.9 is a required update for older versions.
